key_insight: Moment matching alone gives a quantified but limited approximation to Haar-random output probabilities; adding local invariance sharply improves the full distributional accuracy.
engineering_relevance: For quantum circuit designers, this clarifies when approximate unitary designs are sufficient for randomness-sensitive metrics like output-probability statistics and entropy.
method: Proved Kolmogorov-distance bounds between single-output probabilities of strong approximate unitary k-designs and the finite-dimensional Porter-Thomas law.
Showed the bound scales as O(sqrt(2^n/(k(k+2^n))) + ε) and is optimal up to constants.
Identified extra local translation invariance on O(log k) qubits as a structure that improves errors to 2^{-Ω(k)} in Kolmogorov distance and total variation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical guarantees and optimality results, not an empirical benchmark, with additional entropy-error bounds derived from the distributional distance result.
watch_item: The strongest improvements require extra local invariance beyond generic approximate k-designs, so standard design constructions may not achieve the exponential error decay.
paper_title: Random Quantum Circuits Beyond Moment Matching
